requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`, so it needs no implementation evidence. It has no `Implements` edges and no review roots were supplied.

Each clause constrains only what a provider request contains, not how the code is built:
- "every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt ... and another at the end of its last message": a different builder, a post-processing pass over the request, or a different library would send the same request, so the construction is discretionary.
- "Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request": this is a property of the request content.
- For OpenAI, "MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests", "replay prior conversation content in its original order" and "MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks": these are also properties of the request. They do not prescribe a type, signature, field, library or named interface.

The requirement cites `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` only for context. The text names no required library, algorithm, signature or delegation. Whether the requests behave as described is a behavioral question, so I left it to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover every behavioral obligation of `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Explicit-checkpoint backends (Bedrock)**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a two-request conversation against a caching Claude model. The second request follows a reasoning turn.
- For every request it asserts that the system array is `[text, cachePoint]`. The system text starts with `# Task`, so the checkpoint comes right after the system prompt.
- It asserts that the last message's final block is the checkpoint, and that the body contains exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences. That rules out extra or stale checkpoints.
- "Checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request" is checked by comparing each cached body, with the checkpoints stripped by `without_cache_points`, against the body from a non-caching model (`fixture-uncached-model`). It also asserts that the non-caching model's body has no `cachePoint`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` covers the "backend and model support" condition. `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude and Nova, including an ARN, and false for Llama and an unknown model. It also checks that `place_cache_checkpoints` only sets the cache option and leaves the rest of the request unchanged, including after a reasoning turn.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_continues_when_the_model_refuses_a_checkpoint_after_reasoning]` covers the case where a model rejects a checkpoint after a reasoning turn. The conversation continues, and the follow-up keeps the system checkpoint but has no message checkpoint. I read this as the model not supporting a checkpoint in that situation. The requirement's conditional wording allows that reading.

**OpenAI**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` covers the unchanged-prefix obligations. Both requests have identical `instructions` and `tools`.
- The second request's input starts with exactly the first request's input, followed by the function call and then its output, in the original order.
- `assert_no_checkpoints` recursively rejects `cachePoint`, `cache_control` and checkpoint-typed blocks in every request.

The requirement's reference to the system prompt being the same across assessments of a kind comes from the cited `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts`. That requirement is not reassessed here. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no unresolved gaps.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
structural requirement review, behavioral requirement review, distributed
requirement review, example, citation review, and site review. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
